summary: WorldEntity generation-9 candidate PR #437 inherits generation-8's 65536-byte aggregate canonical metadata retention budget, but oversized caller metadata is still scanned without a project-owned work bound before that budget rejects it. checkedNonEmpty() calls assertNonEmpty(), which executes string.find(value, '%c') on kind and origin worldId/regionId/generator/recipeKey before assertCanonicalMetadataBudget() runs. This makes the negative validation path linear in arbitrary caller string size and undercuts #429's O(1) validation claim. WorldEntity.isId() already demonstrates the safer order by length-fencing to 256 before the control-character scan, and persistentState has explicit bounded preflight work. Have the active WorldEntity lineage add a primitive-type plus aggregate-byte preflight before metadata content scans, preserving the aggregate contract rather than inventing arbitrary per-field truncation; add exact-boundary/+1 and source-order/adversarial coverage. Do not spawn a competing primary while generation 9 owns REALITY-CONTRACT.
evidence: PR #437 exact head fef576fea1a7daffa6c8df0868703ce203ad5388 is the live generation-9 WorldEntity primary and is based on generation-8 PR #429's canonical metadata budget repair.

On #437, checkedNonEmpty() asserts string type then calls assertNonEmpty(); assertNonEmpty() rejects control characters via string.find(value, '%c'). cloneOrigin() runs checkedNonEmpty() for worldId, optional regionId, generator, and recipeKey, and ownRecord()/new() run it for kind.

assertCanonicalMetadataBudget(kind, origin) is called only after cloneOrigin() and kind checkedNonEmpty() have completed, so a string many megabytes larger than the 65536-byte aggregate budget can be scanned before deterministic rejection.

WorldEntity.isId() checks #value <= 256 before string.find(value, '%c'), bounding its scan, while cloneState() explicitly bounds root traversal/node/string work; the metadata path is therefore inconsistent with established bounded-work patterns in the same module.

PR #429 describes canonical metadata validation as O(1) five-string length accounting; that is true for the final aggregate arithmetic but not for the preceding unbounded control-character scans on hostile oversized input.

PR #437 currently has no review submissions or comments, and repository PR search found no separate metadata-preflight/bounded-scan successor. No Roblox Studio, engine, viewport, physical-contact, or two-client evidence is implicated or claimed.
